newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds issuance seen increasing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds issuance seen increasing.

text.p: The pace of corporate bond issuance is expected to heat up once more as issuers tempted by lower rates are lured from the sidelines, dealers said.
"The pace is beginning to pick up...we're beginning to hear a few names," one syndicate source said.
Dealers said earlier in the week that players were seen checking historical trading spreads as U.S. Treasury yields fell after the Federal Reserve's decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
So far on Friday, Ford Motor priced $500 million in 12-year notes to yield 69 basis points over U.S. Treasuries
The following deals are expected to price but no official dates have been set, dealers said.
Union Pacific Resources is expected to price a $400 million A3/A-rated two-part debt offering consisting of $200 million in 10-year debt and $200 million in 30-year debt.
Medpartners is also expected to tap the market with $300 million in Baa3/BBB rated 10-year debt via Smith Barney.
Petronas is expected to price $1.0 billion in five and 10-year debt in early October, dealers said.
British Sky Broadcasting is rumoured to bring debt to market via Goldman Sachs & Co, sources said.
Loewen Group is expected to price $350 million in a two-part senior guaranteed notes deal consisting of $175 million five-year debt and $175 million seven-year debt via Smith Barney.

In addition, South Africa is gearing up to launch its first yankee issue ever via Merrill Lynch & Co, syndicate sources added. The deal is expected to consist of $250 to $300 million of a 10-year maturity.
Also, Brazil may issue a $750 million global bond next week consisting of five and ten-year maturities, syndicate managers said.
"Everyone is extremely interested in this because Brazil is such a rare Euromarket borrower," said one syndicate manager.
Dealers said with very little Brazilian sovereign debt outstanding in the Eurobond market, and no emerging market 10-year dollar bonds, spread talk on the issues would be difficult to peg.
Argentina has also decided to tap the markets with $750 million in a 10-year global debt via Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers.
Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Friday that the country had no plans to increase the global deal announced earlier in the day.
"For the time being, we have only the $750 million issue," Fernandez said at a press conference in New York. "Later, we will see...these things are permanently under study."
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 6/32 at 98-15/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
